claims.text: Need to add `field` to the imports: `from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field`
Is src/sentry/integrations/services/ the right home for AssignmentSource, given the rest of that directory is hybrid-cloud RPC service layer and AssignmentSource is a plain non-RPC frozen dataclass?
Ruff flags both parameters (attribute, sync_source) as unused in the default should_sync implementation, which may cause CI lint failures

The new assignment_source parameter added to IssueSyncIntegration.sync_status_outbound has no producer and no consumer anywhere in the repo, and its declared signature is incompatible with ExampleIntegration's implementation, which doesn't even accept **kwargs.
ExampleIntegration.sync_status_outbound method lacks **kwargs and will raise TypeError when called with the new assignment_source parameter
Method name says 'empty_array' but tests empty dict - consider renaming to 'test_from_dict_empty_dict' for clarity.

No test verifies that a different integration still propagates changes outward — only the same-integration blocking case is tested — so an inverted guard condition (blocking everything instead of only the matching source) would still pass all existing tests.

Does the same-integration loop guard actually stop a multi-integration back-and-forth (A → Sentry → B → Sentry → A) when two or more issue-sync integrations are linked to the same group, and which loop originally motivated this fix?
to_dict() returns a datetime for queued; if this dict is passed in task kwargs (e.g., via apply_async), JSON serialization may fail depending on the serializer, which can cause enqueue errors.
Shared mutable default in dataclass timestamp

The new test exercises the guard by calling GroupAssignee.objects.assign(assignment_source=...) directly rather than through the real entry point sync_group_assignee_inbound, so the actual end-to-end behavior ("webhook comes in → no outbound re-send to the same integration") remains untested.

AssignmentSource.from_dict swallows parse failures and returns None; since the caller treats None as "no source" and the guard is `if sync_source and ...`, a parse failure silently disables the outbound-sync loop protection with no logging or metric to reveal it happened.
The deassign-direction loop guard (matching source) has no corresponding test.
The method name has a typo: test_from_dict_inalid_data should be test_from_dict_invalid_data.

The ~30-45 line integration + ExternalIssue + GroupLink test setup is now duplicated verbatim for the third time by this PR's new test, triggering the Rule of Three, and risks silent drift since the 5-key sync config dict must stay consistent across every copy.

During a rolling deploy, will the retry configuration on sync_assignee_outbound tolerate the window where new code enqueues an assignment_source_dict kwarg that old workers' function signature can't accept (causing a TypeError)?

test_to_dict only asserts that queued `is not None`, an assertion too weak to catch the shared-default-timestamp bug described in F-001 even though this test is the only place that exercises the queued field.

The `assignment_source` parameter added to the `sync_status_outbound` abstract method is never passed by the `sync_status_outbound` task and has no effect today - it's unused dead code that should either have a TODO comment or be removed
